purpose: Design references for manuals: bestiaries, rulebooks and pocket field manuals, read for how a page teaches. Opened 2026-11-16 beside the AC '26 Magician's Manual (papers/arxiv-magicians-manual).
posture: Index and citation only. Public-domain and openly licensed PDFs are fetched into sources/ (gitignored) by fetch-sources.mjs from the Internet Archive and the publisher; nothing is mirrored into the repo. In-copyright commercial books (the TSR and GDW originals) are cited and never fetched, though unlicensed scans of them are easy to find.

checked_key.true: title, date, host and rights line read from the host's own record during the 2026-11-16 pass
checked_key.false: written from working knowledge; wants a verification pass before it is cited in a paper

shelves.ancestor: Public-domain books the game manual descends from: demon dictionaries, bestiaries, war-game rules, field manuals.
shelves.open: Modern role-playing rulebooks under open licences or given away by their authors.
shelves.cite-only: The in-copyright originals. Named so the lineage is complete; not fetched.

sources.title: Dictionnaire infernal: répertoire universel des êtres, des personnages, des livres, des faits et des choses qui tiennent aux esprits
sources.rights: Public domain. Library of Congress scan.
sources.why: The monster manual before the monster manual: an alphabetical dictionary of demons, one entry per being, with a wood-engraved portrait dropped into the column beside the name. The entry-plus-portrait unit is the same one the 1977 Monster Manual uses.

sources.title: The History of Four-footed Beasts and Serpents
sources.rights: Public domain. Duke University Libraries scan.
sources.why: An English bestiary where real and fabulous animals get the same treatment: a woodcut, then names, habitat, habits and uses under running heads. A stat block in prose, 320 years early.

sources.title: Little Wars: a game for boys from twelve years of age to one hundred and fifty and for that more intelligent sort of girl who likes boys' games and books
sources.rights: Public domain. New York Public Library scan.
sources.why: A rulebook written as a story of how the rules were found, with marginal drawings and photographs of play. The voice a manual can have when one person wrote it for friends.

sources.title: Rules for the Conduct of the War-Game on a Map
sources.rights: Public domain. California Digital Library scan.
sources.why: The institutional rulebook: numbered paragraphs, tables, an umpire. The dry register tabletop rules inherited and the form Traveller's little black books look most like.

authors: United States. Office of Strategic Services
sources.title: Simple Sabotage Field Manual: Strategic Services (Provisional)
sources.venue: Washington, D.C.: Office of Strategic Services, Strategic Services Field Manual No. 3
sources.why: A pocket manual: typewritten, numbered to three levels, no pictures, meant to be carried and acted on. The opposite pole from the illustrated bestiary.

sources.title: System Reference Document 5.1
sources.venue: Renton, WA: Wizards of the Coast
sources.why: Current Dungeons & Dragons rules and monsters under an open licence, straight from the publisher. Two columns, stat blocks, no art: the skeleton of the commercial books.

sources.title: Basic Fantasy Role-Playing Game Core Rules, 3rd Edition (Release 97)
sources.rights: Distributed free by its author; open game content. Internet Archive mirror.
sources.why: A free game laid out on purpose like the early-1980s boxed rules: one typeface, line art, tables set in the text column. The closest legal stand-in for the look of the old books.

sources.title: The Basic Fantasy Field Guide of Creatures Malevolent and Benign (Release 22)
sources.rights: Distributed free by its authors; open game content. Internet Archive mirror.
sources.why: A community-made monster book in the classic form: name, stat table, paragraph, drawing.

sources.title: OSRIC: Old School Reference and Index Compilation, Core Rules v2.2
sources.rights: Free PDF from its authors under the Open Game License. Internet Archive mirror.
sources.why: A restatement of first-edition Advanced D&D, monsters and all, that can be read and shared freely.

sources.title: Advanced Dungeons & Dragons Monster Manual
sources.rights: In copyright and sold today. Cite it; never mirror it. Scans circulate on the Internet Archive without the rights holder's licence and this platter does not fetch them.
sources.why: The book the request named. Alphabetical monsters, each a block of statistics, a paragraph and a small ink drawing.

sources.title: Advanced Dungeons & Dragons Dungeon Masters Guide
sources.rights: In copyright and sold today. Cite it; never mirror it. Scans circulate on the Internet Archive without the rights holder's licence and this platter does not fetch them.
sources.why: The dense one: tables on nearly every page, appendices, an author talking to the reader throughout.

sources.title: Dungeons & Dragons Basic Rulebook
sources.rights: In copyright and sold today. Cite it; never mirror it. Scans circulate on the Internet Archive without the rights holder's licence and this platter does not fetch them.
sources.why: Sixty-four pages meant to teach a newcomer from nothing. The nearest precedent for a short manual that orders rules by what a player does first.

sources.title: Traveller, Books 1 to 3: Characters and Combat; Starships; Worlds and Adventures
sources.rights: In copyright and sold today. Cite it; never mirror it. Scans circulate on the Internet Archive without the rights holder's licence and this platter does not fetch them. Far Future Enterprises has offered a facsimile edition; whether it is free was not checked.
sources.why: The little black books: digest size, black covers with one line of type, no illustration, numbered procedures and tables.

sources.title: Cepheus Engine System Reference Document
sources.rights: Open Game License, sold pay-what-you-want behind a storefront login. Free to fetch by hand into sources/; not fetched by the script.
sources.why: The open restatement of classic Traveller, for when the rules themselves are wanted.
